tagline: Plot is not what happens. It is why the next thing must.

epigraph.text: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
epigraph.cite: Charles Dickens, A Tale of Two Cities (1859)

art.note: The council approved a single indigo knot on unbleached rag cotton with an equal four-second silence, rejecting additional color or decoration.

writers.note: One indigo knot and a four-second pause: the room follows cause, not spectacle.

nuggets.hook: A knot can hide a whole story in one pull.
nuggets.body: Pull one thread and the whole pattern tightens. A plot begins when something has to follow.

nuggets.hook: The queen died of a broken heart. The king died of the why.
nuggets.body: A plot is a chain of causes, not a line of events. The word because turns a sequence into a story.

nuggets.hook: A story can start at the top of the mountain.
nuggets.body: Some plots begin after the climb, on the long way down. The shape decides what the struggle means.

nuggets.hook: Four seconds of silence can hold the whole twist.
nuggets.body: Before the reveal, the room waits. A twist is a promise kept in the first lines.
